classification.difficultyReason: Combine opposite percentage changes to two dimensions to determine the new area without knowing either original dimension.

content.prompt: The length of a rectangle is increased by $15\%$ and the width decreased by $10\%$. If the area of the original rectangle is $100\text{ cm}^2$, find the area of the new rectangle.

answer.short:
$103.5\text{ cm}^2$.

Multiply the original area by the length factor $1.15$ and the width factor $0.90$.
answer.worked:
Let the original length and width be $l$ and $w$ centimetres, so $lw=100$.

$$\begin{align*}l_{\text{new}}&=l+\frac{15}{100}l\\l_{\text{new}}&=1.15l\\w_{\text{new}}&=w-\frac{10}{100}w\\w_{\text{new}}&=0.90w\\A_{\text{new}}&=(1.15l)(0.90w)\\A_{\text{new}}&=1.035lw\\A_{\text{new}}&=1.035\times100\\A_{\text{new}}&=103.5\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
